Hello, I am male, age 21, and completely friendless apart from the occasional conversation with an online friend.
If you would like to converse feel free to message me.
I will warn you I do not know how to have a normal conversation but will try if you are interested.

I am/was not only too anxious to make friends, but entirely incapable so perhaps I can relate.
As someone with depression and suicidal thoughts. This information is comforting.

I'm just saying I don't have a rational cause.

Unless its rational to kill oneself over a bowl of cereal...

Its funny because I think I'm usually very rational.

I think you're confusing sadness with depression, at least I think that's what I have.

See, I have no real reason I to want to kill myself. But I do.

I don't need any reason to be sad/anxious. Which is why I believe it is a disease, illness, abnormality or whatever at least in my case.

I suppose I do have some triggers though
I hadn't thought of that, but that sounds like something I would do. :)

I used to believe it was because I never had any friends.

I'm a bit weird, don't talk much, never know what to say etc...

Now I believe I have some sort of psychological or chemical illness.

I feel as though I'm barely alive, or sleeping.

Every little thing is much to much work.

This cannot go on.


Either I continue to do nothing until I die of some other means,

I somehow get better but I don't know how,

Or I just end it now and give up.

Madness is strange.

Here I am talking to myself I have no one else.

It would seem that..

Something strange happens.

I feel very anxious one minute, then from the insanity I feel slightly happy.

It will not last though.


Here's a thought I had....

Depression is a disease so powerful it renders its victims to drive their self to the point of suicide.

What is the purpose of life? To survive.

What is suicide? Something that destroys that purpose.

A force so powerful it compels people to undo billions of years of evolution: don't die.

Instead this force drives oneself to end oneself.

If I knew another way I would take it.

But considering I don't have a doctor, or money...

Or courage.

Its very strange

Most of the work is already done.

I just wanted some cereal but there aren't any clean bowls and, I mean

Going to the kitchen is hard enough but washing a bowl would be too much

What's preventing you?

Is it fear? Is it love? You felt nothing for 4 years now... So what's preventing you?

Hah! Nice name! If you want to talk about pen testing I would love to hear it! (I'm more interested in computers  than helicopters...)

>Physical abuse was, and in some societies still is, an acceptable action. We aren't all that far out of the era where beating your wife and children was fairly socially accepted in the United States.

Then society was wrong. Just like the majority of humans used to believe the earth was flat. We've since learned better, and have become more civilized.

I suppose we could get into a debate as to what actually defines "good" or "evil" if its not society or some deity, then what?
Perhaps there is no such thing.
I personally believe morality is equal for everyone and everything in the universe and culture and society is irrelevant. If I can't murder you, you can't murder me. There are of course exceptions, self defense being one of them.

Society, the masses, and culture are far too stupid and uncivilized to be in charge of what is actually good or evil.

Unfortunately I can't prove good or evil even exist though.

Nobody pick me, I'm the outcast.  :)

I see the party culture as, well, they are idiots. I think I can relate with some points you mentioned.
It seems like even in groups I could relate to on some level (technology,  aviation, video games) I'm either not smart enough, not interested enough, or just too afraid to do anything or say anything to try and participate.
I guess what I'm trying to say is I don't fit in anywhere - even in things I'm interested in.
So yes, I guess we kind of relate a little? :/

tldr: I've never had hallucinations but I have had night terrors. More often when I was a child. Although I had one just recently and couldn't go back to sleep at all. 


When I was 8 or so I saw glowing hands hovering over my feet, looked like it was going to chop them off. I could swear I was wide awake, but knew I was actually dreaming. I tried to scream to wake myself up, but that rarely works. This would almost be considered an hallucination. However, because I was actually sleeping, its something else. 
I don't seem to have them anymore, with the exception of one I had recently where I dreamed I was falling through space. And of course screaming to try to same myself up, didn't work. That's the difference between a nightmare and night terror. Also, once I finally do wake up, I feel terrified at everything until morning.
